Every run read SKILL.md first.

Rules changed since 0397dec (git diff 0397dec -- idiomatic-elixir/): of the case's seven rules, two changed. (1) Update structs with `%{struct | field: value}` gained "In `defstruct`, list a field whose default is `nil` as a bare atom, `defstruct [:items, :discount]`, not `discount: nil`; a keyword entry is for a real default, such as `items: %{}`." That sentence decides each run's defstruct line, graded as in sweeps/2026-10-22-check-6/grades/shop-project-skill.json: opus-1 line 7 `defstruct [:items, :discount]`, haiku-1 line 7 `defstruct [:items, :code]`, haiku-2 line 9 `defstruct [:items, :discount]`, sonnet-1 line 9 `defstruct [:items, :discount]`, sonnet-2 line 9 `defstruct [:items, :discount]`. All five list the nil-default field as a bare atom, so all are clean, and four are the rule's own example word for word. That is 0 of 5, against 4 of 5 in 2026-10-22-b and 0 of 4 in check-6. The same caveat as check-6 applies: the starting cart.ex already had `defstruct [:items]`. The rule's first two sentences are unchanged and graded as before. Map.put/3 on the inner items map inside %{cart | items: ...} is not the pattern the rule forbids. (2) Before you finish, step 4, gained "While you work on one module, `mix test test/my_app/orders_test.exs` runs only its tests, `mix test test/my_app/orders_test.exs:42` the one test at that line, and `mix test --failed` the tests that failed last time. Run the whole suite once more before you finish, since a change in one module can break a test in another." The last sentence now decides the test step.

Before you finish, what each session ran (0 of 5 violated). No run used a single-file form, a :line form or --failed. Every mix test was a bare `mix test`, the full suite, and in every run the last mix test was a full run with no edit after it. opus-1: after its last edit, one chain `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && mix compile --warnings-as-errors 2>&1 | tail -5 && mix credo --strict 2>&1 | tail -8 && mix test 2>&1 | tail -8`, with no warnings, no Credo issues and 19 passed; the full test run came last. haiku-1: `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force 2>&1 | tail -20 && mix test 2>&1 | tail -30` (14 passed), then `mix credo --strict 2>&1 | tail -15` (no issues); its only test run was full and nothing was edited after it. haiku-2: a full `mix test` before editing (3 passed), then after its edits `mix format && mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force 2>&1 | tail -5 && mix test 2>&1 | tail -30 && mix credo --strict 2>&1 | tail -30` (15 passed, no issues). sonnet-1: a refused python3 heredoc that had carried the checks, then after two Write calls `mix format; mix compile --warnings-as-errors 2>&1 | tail; mix test 2>&1 | tail -15; mix credo --strict 2>&1 | tail -15` (19 passed, no issues). sonnet-2: a refused python3 heredoc that carried `mix format && mix test`, then after a Write and two Edits `mix format && mix test 2>&1 | tail -20` and `mix credo --strict 2>&1 | tail -15`. The test output shows `==> shop / Compiling 1 file (.ex) / Generated shop app` with no warnings and 19 passed, and Credo found no issues.

Before you finish, judgment call: sonnet-2 never ran a separate `mix compile`, though mix test compiled the app with no warnings. This is the shape 2026-10-22-b graded clean for its sonnet-1, so this grade also calls it clean to keep the sweeps comparable. A stricter reading that requires the literal command would turn Sonnet to violated. Check-6's violated sonnet-2 differs: that run never ran Credo.

Chain fallible steps with `with`: no run's final lib file contains a `with`, so the rule is not exercised in any run. Each single fallible call uses case: opus-1 lines 75-78, haiku-1 lines 53-56, haiku-2 lines 55-58, sonnet-1 lines 85-88, sonnet-2 lines 76-79 and 101-104. Sonnet-2's refused python3 draft had one-step `with` blocks in apply_code/2 and total/2, the public shape the rule names. The Write that replaced the draft wrote case in both places, so the output does not break the rule. Its text is unchanged since 0397dec, and 2026-10-22-b had 1 of 5 (sonnet-1).

The other rules' text is unchanged since 0397dec and they are graded to the 2026-10-22-b standard: Convert external strings to atoms, Return {:ok, value} or {:error, reason}, Store and compute money, Naming. A total function that raises KeyError on an unpriced SKU counts as clean under the return-tuple rule when its @doc says so (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1). Sonnet-2 returns {:error, {:unknown_sku, sku}} instead. Under Naming, haiku-1 calls the typed string `input` and the parsed atom `code`. The rule's list of generic names (data, item, res, x) does not include `input`, and earlier grades let `value` and `result` pass, so this is clean.

Expected reads: all five runs added tests. Opus-1 and sonnet-1 read testing.md and library-design.md (with cat) before their first edit. Haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 read SKILL.md only (reads field, and no testing.md text in their transcripts beyond SKILL.md's own mention), so they missed the expected read. In 2026-10-22-b only haiku-1 missed it.

other_violations, mostly from testing.md sentences added since 0397dec, which the three runs that skipped testing.md broke. Haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 write bare `{:ok, cart} = ...` arrange matches in test bodies. That breaks Assert with patterns' new sentence "In a test body, every match that can fail takes `assert` in front, the arrange steps included". Haiku-1 and haiku-2 also bind and then `==` a field, the rule's older "Instead of" shape. Haiku-1 (line 83) and haiku-2 (line 95) pipe two steps on one line (`code |> String.trim() |> String.upcase()`), and opus-1 has single-step pipes in two doctests (lines 36 and 94), as earlier grades listed under the pipeline rule. I found no break of the do: rule. Opus-1 and sonnet-2 write a one-expression second clause of apply_*/2 as a block beside a case block, which is two clauses, not "most". I found no test with the expected value on the left of `==`.

Verified in scratch copies of each run's project (copied with its .formatter.exs, then mix deps.get): mix format --check-formatted, mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors, mix credo --strict (no issues) and mix test pass in all five. Test counts: opus-1 19 (3 doctests), haiku-1 14, haiku-2 15, sonnet-1 19 (3 doctests), sonnet-2 19 (4 doctests). Results of a mix run probe: 2 x APPLE at 100 gives 699, 679 with SAVE10 and 200 with FREESHIP in all five (sonnet-2 as {:ok, cents}). Opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 reject a second code, and the Haiku runs replace it. Removing 5 of 2 units empties the items. BOGUS returns a tagged-tuple reason in all five. The Haiku runs trim and upcase the code; the others are case-sensitive. An unpriced SKU raises KeyError except in sonnet-2, which returns {:error, {:unknown_sku, "KIWI"}}. No lib file has String.to_atom/1 or a float.
